age.evidence: 108 male Wistar rats (180-200 g, 8-9 weeks old)

dosing.doses_raw: 25 mg/kg in a volume of 1 mL
dosing.evidence: Psilocybe cubensis was injected intraperitoneal at the dose of 25 mg/kg (single administration) before (pretrain) or after (posttrain) shocks, or before the test (pretest).

group_housing.evidence: The rats were housed six per Plexiglas cage (25 × 50 × 25 cm)

day_night_flipped.evidence: a 12 hr:12 hr light/dark cycle (lights on at 7:00 hr) ... all the experiments were done during the light hours (9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.)

enrichment_housing.evidence: No mention of enrichment in home cage.

assays.assay_description: Plexiglas chamber (30 × 25 × 30 cm) with shock-grid floor. Rats received 3 tone-shock pairings (75 dB, 3 s tone; 0.8 mA, 3 s shock); on test day (1, 3, or 21 days later) tone presented 3 times (30 s interval) without shock; freezing (episodes >1 s of no movement) was manually scored.

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were placed on the apparatus again ... freezing rate was manually measured

food_restriction.evidence: No food present in fear-conditioning chamber; rats had free access to food in home cage.

water_restriction.evidence: No water present in chamber during test.

time_to_assay.evidence: pretrain (1 hr before shocks), posttrain (5 min after shocks), or pretest (1 hr before test); test performed 1, 3, or 21 days after conditioning

sample_size.evidence: Each experimental group consisted of six rats ... 18 experimental groups (n = 6)

outcomes.summary: Pre- or post-train Psilocybe cubensis (25 mg/kg) potently decreased freezing 1 and 3 days after fear conditioning, but not at 21 days. Pre-test administration decreased freezing only at 1 day.
outcomes.statistics: Psilocybe cubensis F(1,90)=325.57, p<.001; injection time F(2,90)=7.29, p<.001; days F(2,90)=128.12, p<.001; 3-way interaction F(4,90)=3.96, p=.005; Dunnett post-hoc p<.001
outcomes.evidence: pre- or posttrain Psilocybe cubensis potently decreased PTSD-like behavior after 1 or 3 days but not 21 days of shock exposure (p < .001) ... Pretest Psilocybe cubensis decreased PTSD-like behavior only after 1 day of shock exposure

B1_num_measures.evidence: The freezing rate (episodes over > 1 s of no movement) was manually measured

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single total freezing rate reported, no within-session time-binning.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No transition or sequence analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Conditioned freezing is not counted as ethological in this rubric.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Fear conditioning requires learned tone-shock association.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: freezing rate was manually measured by experimenter

D1_continuity.evidence: Each rat tested on one of days 1, 3, or 21 (one recording session for that animal).

D2_session_duration.evidence: Three tone presentations with 30 s intervals; total session well under 15 min.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Each cohort tested on a single day (1, 3, or 21 days post-conditioning); no baseline pre-test was recorded.

D5_followup.evidence: Tests performed at 1, 3, or 21 days after last drug injection (≥24 h for many groups).

assays.assay_description: Clear perspex box (30 × 30 × 40 cm) divided into 16 squares. Locomotor activity (number of square crossings) and anxiety (time in 4 middle squares) manually scored over 300 s. Conducted 60 min after fear-conditioning test on day 1, 3, or 21.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats moved freely in the open field box.

time_to_assay.evidence: Drug administered pretrain (1 h pre-shocks), posttrain (5 min post-shocks), or pretest (1 h pre-test); OFT performed 60 min after fear test on day 1, 3, or 21.

sample_size.evidence: Each experimental group consisted of six rats; all six rats in each group used for all tests.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybe cubensis decreased locomotor activity at 1 and 3 days (pretrain/posttrain) and at all timepoints (pretest), but not at 21 days for pre/posttrain. Anxiety (time in middle squares) was increased only at 21 days for pretrain/posttrain groups.
outcomes.statistics: Locomotor: Psilocybe cubensis F(1,90)=530.78, p<.001; 3-way interaction F(4,90)=8.00, p<.001. Anxiety: main effect F(1,90)=1.86, p>.05; Psilocybe Cubensis × Days F(2,90)=19.46, p<.001; 3-way F(4,90)=6.09, p<.001.
outcomes.evidence: pre- or posttrain Psilocybe cubensis potently decreased locomotor activity after 1 or 3 days but not 21 days ... Pretest Psilocybe cubensis decreased locomotor activity in all groups ... pre- or posttrain Psilocybe cubensis potently decreased anxiety-like behavior only after [21] days

B1_num_measures.evidence: number of crossings ... time spent in the four middle squares

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total counts over 300 s session; no time-binning.

B4_ethological.evidence: Crossings and centre time are spatial measures, not ethological acts.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: The scores were manually measured by experimenter

D2_session_duration.evidence: Locomotor activity was evaluated ... during 300 s

D3_recording_days.evidence: Each cohort tested on a single day (1, 3, or 21 days post-conditioning).

D5_followup.evidence: Some cohorts tested 3 or 21 days after last drug administration.

assays.assay_description: Hot plate at 50 °C with 120 s cutoff. Latency to paw-lick or step change (pain subthreshold) automatically recorded. Performed 10 min after OFT on day 1, 3, or 21.

setup_restrain.evidence: rat was placed on the hot sheet (no restraint described)

time_to_assay.evidence: Drug given pretrain/posttrain/pretest; hot plate ran 10 min after OFT (~70 min after fear test) on day 1, 3, or 21.

sample_size.evidence: Each experimental group consisted of six rats; all six rats used for all tests.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybe cubensis (25 mg/kg) significantly increased pain subthreshold (longer latency to nociceptive response) in all injection-timing groups and at all test timepoints (1, 3, 21 days).
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybe cubensis in all groups potently increased pain subthreshold (p < .001) in comparison with its' related saline group

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Device records latency timing only; no behavioural classifier.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Hot plate apparatus was a sheet getting hot by electric current

D3_recording_days.evidence: Each cohort tested on a single day (1, 3, or 21 days post-conditioning).

D5_followup.evidence: Cohorts tested 3 or 21 days after last drug injection.

judge_notes: Three distinct behavioural paradigms identified: Fear Conditioning Test (freezing recall), Open Field Test (locomotor + anxiety zone measures), and Hot Plate Test. All three are scored as separate assays (different apparatuses, different behavioural domains).
Per rubric, all dose-timing variants (pretrain/posttrain/pretest) and test-day variants (1, 3, 21 days) of each test are collapsed into one assay entry.

D3 (recording days) corrected to 1 for each assay: each animal cohort was tested on a SINGLE day (1, 3, or 21 days post-conditioning); different cohorts ≠ multiple recording days for one assay. Candidates qwen/glm/gptoss over-counted this.
D1 corrected to 'Single session': each rat undergoes one recording per assay; no baseline pre-test was performed.
B1 for Fear Conditioning: freezing rate is a single measure (score 0, category '1'). Glm's score of 1 was inconsistent with rubric (1 measure → 0 pts).
OFT outcome direction set to 'mixed' because locomotor decreased while anxiety-related centre time increased at 21 days.
Housing handling and enrichment marked 'not_reported' (paper silent).
